utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Do I understand that there is a matter you wish to raise, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. This time there is something that I would like to ask the Trial Chamber in view of the holidays coming in April. As you well know, Easter is a religious holiday celebrated across Serbia; however, it falls a little later as compared to the rest of Europe and Christendom. This year Good Friday falls on the 17th and the Easter Monday on the 20th. Therefore, I would like to ask the Chamber to make sure that those two days will not be working days and that we shall not be sitting on those two days. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That appears to be a week later than the Christian, Western Good Friday and Easter Monday, the Eastern Orthodox is this year a week later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are entirely right, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I wonder how counsel are seeing the progress of the case and how we will be placed by then, as both you're here, Mr. Stamp, and Mr. Djurdjic. Have you given any thought to the rate of progress we are making?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're the lucky man first, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I rose quickly because I have very little to say. We have given thought to it but to be precise in our calculations I couldn't do it off the bat. I think we are making very good progress, and a lot would to some degree depend on the Court's decision in respect to the 92 bis application. Of course the Court might want to hear more evidence before finally deciding on that, but I think by the end of March/early April we should be approaching halfway in number of the witnesses or we should have passed halfway in number of witnesses who are 65 -- who are 92 ter witnesses or live witnesses. However, some of the more, shall I say, involved witnesses might take a little bit longer -- are yet to come. But in a general -- my general position is that we are making very good, if not excellent, progress. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber is a little more concerned than you are I think, Mr. Stamp. We felt, as everybody knows, we had a slowish start for a number of reasons, and we have been improving in our progress. But we are now at the 20th witness, and I think your list exceeds or will now exceed 120 witnesses, which means we are a long way from even halfway. The 92 bis decision is imminent. Not a great deal of difference will be made on the outcome of that decision one way or the other, really. It just saves some time in examination-in-chief. There will be some few witnesses for no cross-examination, but it's not going to transform the length of the case in a major way. So what I think pre-trial was seen as a trial that might end in eight or nine months is looking like a trial that will last much longer than that. Is that something entirely astray from your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If -- and it's really a matter for discretion of this Court. If we have to call all the witnesses for cross-examination, it would take -- probably longer than that -- not probably, it certainly would be longer than that. I think on this side we have to make efforts to stay within the time that we indicated we would if we're allowed to call these witnesses for cross we should utilise the time we use for the orientation exercise and there may be additional questions -- well, we should optimise that time as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can we say so for Ms. Kravetz is here and Mr. Neuner receive our gold stars for keeping to time. So there's a little room for you to improve there, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Okay, thank you. Mr. Djurdjic, time, have you given any thought to this at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. First and foremost, it is not that I necessarily wish to side with the Prosecutor; however, since the early pre-trial stage, specifically the month of September, I think Mr. Stamp has been talking about a time that was much longer than the Pre-Trial Judge was prepared to allow for. The time is simply too short to have a fair trial. On a number of occasions, Mr. Stamp for that very reason submitted motions that were obviously not approved. So it is quite obvious that some sort of a time schedule had been drawn up by this time. I do not think the time specified is realistic; nevertheless, I am exceptionally happy with the pace of the trial itself. As a result, the Defence has no objections in terms of the way the trial has been run so far; quite the contrary in fact. We do wish to take this opportunity to express our satisfaction. As for the motion to have those two days reserved for celebration, I did this on purpose today just in order to stay in keeping with the general dynamics and in order to avoid any technical issues that might turn up or any potential obstacles to the work of the Chamber. This might even help us to work even more efficiently in the future. We for our part shall try to work as efficiently as possible and address no more than the essential issues; nevertheless, that depends to a large extent also on the OTP and the way they will be going about having their 92 ter statements admitted and what they will single out as appropriate subjects for cross-examination. The example that springs to mind is the two witnesses who are victims, Saranda and Fatos Bogujevci, and that could have been wrapped up much sooner had it not been some statements that were appearing that were interesting for the OTP, so issues kept cropping up leaving us with no choice but to raise further issues on cross. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, the Chamber is concerned that some cross-examination so far have gone longer than was really necessary. I think the tendency is for things to improve, but the important things in the trial, if they're focused on, I think cross-examination could still be shorter. As a simple example, for most witnesses we are not likely to pay any attention to the early education and experience of a witness because those things in most cases are not going to be of any relevance to our consideration of the evidence of a witness. So it could be possible, for example, to leave entirely alone for most witnesses, if not all, the question of the early education and early experience of the witness. Now, I just use that as one example that comes to mind. We are, though, I think encouraged by what you have said, Mr. Djurdjic, and also Mr. Stamp, that each of you are feeling encouraged that the rate of progress is becoming satisfactory and is even improving. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will give some consideration to your proposal, Mr. Djurdjic, and as soon as our position is clear, we will let you know, and we'll try to do that in good time for you to make travel and other arrangements. Thank you. If the witness could now be brought in. Closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 13th day of March, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.59 p.m.,
